findings.where: apps/web/lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts (whole-suite run); cell '630 a stop the door says had ALREADY FINISHED does not re-attach — there is nothing left to read'
findings.what: The final report claims 'whole apps/web unit suite ... 4191 tests, 4189 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped'. A fresh run on this rig (node scripts/run-tests.mjs) measured 4188 pass / 1 fail, and re-running the single file in isolation with the correct bootstrap (node --import ./test/bootstrap.mjs --import tsx --test) is non-deterministic: 2 of 5 isolated runs failed the same cell, 3 passed. This file is untouched by #659 (zero diff vs origin/main) and imports nothing #659 touches, so this is a pre-existing timing flake in #630's thread-stop machinery, not a regression this branch introduced.
findings.evidence: Measured this pass: whole-suite run at /tmp/web-unit.out (`# tests 4191 / # pass 4188 / # fail 1`), failing at apps/web/lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts:1021 (`2 !== 0`, AssertionError). Isolated reruns with `node --import ./test/bootstrap.mjs --import tsx --test lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts`: run A 24/25 (same cell), run B 25/25, run C 25/25, run D 24/25, run E 24/25. `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- apps/web/lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts apps/web/lib/clara/use-clara-thread-stop.ts` is empty (file not in this branch's diff at all).
findings.fix: No action needed on this branch — the flake is unrelated to #659's touched files and reproduces on the branch tip independent of any change here. The final report's 'Report claim vs measured' line should be corrected to '4188 pass, 1 fail (flaky, unrelated: use-clara-thread-stop.test.ts)' rather than '0 fail', per WORK-ORDER rule 6 (claims need a checkable, current measurement). Worth a separate ticket/note for the #630 lane owner since it is non-deterministic under the real bootstrap, not merely under a bad standalone invocation.

findings.what: The client-status chip on the new portfolio table imports `Badge` from `@/components/parts/PartBadge` (a tone-based `neutral|info|warning|error` chip originally built for Clara 'parts' rendering — tool_call chips, clarify labels), not from `@/components/ui/badge.tsx` (the canonical shadcn cva-variant Badge used by most of the rest of the product, e.g. accounting-hub.tsx, members-tables.tsx, bank/accounts-section.tsx). The final report's UI-04 line ('Table ... Pagination, Empty, Skeleton, Badge... no primitive added') reads as claiming the shadcn ui/badge.tsx primitive specifically.
findings.evidence: `grep -n Badge apps/web/components/firm/firm-home/firm-portfolio-section.tsx` -> `import { Badge } from "@/components/parts/PartBadge";` and its one use-site at :286-288. `components/ui/badge.tsx` exists and IS the shadcn cva primitive (verified: cva variants default/secondary/destructive/outline/ghost/link). However every sibling component in the same neighbourhood already standardises on PartBadge's tone chip for the identical purpose: components/firm/client-home/client-work-attention.tsx, components/firm/firm-home/needs-you-scoreboard.tsx, components/firm/firm-home/oldest-waiting-list.tsx, components/tax/SstWatchSection.tsx.
findings.fix: No change needed — this matches, rather than breaks, the established local convention for Firm-altitude status/tone chips (four sibling components in components/firm/* already use PartBadge's Badge for exactly this purpose), so it is consistent reuse rather than a fresh violation or a second chip implementation. Flagging only so the final report's UI-04 evidence line names the actual module (PartBadge, matching its firm-surface siblings) rather than implying components/ui/badge.tsx specifically, since a future reader auditing 'is #659 really using shadcn's Badge' would otherwise be misled by the report text.
